q: How do I disclose group captive or third-party solar in my Scope 2 report?
title: Disclosing captive solar in Scope 2 reports
short: Show two Scope 2 totals side by side, location-based and market-based, and say which one each headline figure uses. Report the solar as renewable electricity in MWh or GJ in your energy table, and add a short method note naming the contract, the units claimed and the factor used for the remaining grid power.
audience: Indian factories with group captive or third-party solar PPAs

sections.h: Captive or third-party makes no difference to the disclosure
p: Whether the solar comes from a group captive plant or a third-party open access PPA changes the charges on your bill, not the carbon reporting. Both are contractual instruments under the GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance. The disclosure below is the same for either; what matters is that the contract gives you the renewable attributes.

sections.h: The lines to show in a GHG inventory
ul: Total electricity consumed, in MWh, split into grid-supplied and contracted solar.
Scope 2 location-based, in t CO2, with the CEA database version and factor.
Scope 2 market-based, in t CO2, with the solar MWh claimed and the factor used for the rest.
The instrument type for the solar (group captive agreement or third-party PPA) and the reporting year the units were adjusted in.
A statement that no RECs or carbon credits were sold for the claimed units.

p: The BRSR format published with SEBI's July 2023 circular asks for energy consumption split into renewable and non-renewable sources, in joules or multiples. Put the adjusted solar units under electricity from renewable sources and the grid units under non-renewable, converting at 3.6 GJ per MWh. BRSR asks for Scope 2 in t CO2e without naming a method, so state in the note whether your figure is location-based or market-based, and keep the same choice each year.

sections.h: A method note you can adapt
p: "Scope 2 is reported on both bases. Location-based applies the CEA CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0 weighted average of 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh to all electricity consumed. Market-based treats [X] MWh of solar, adjusted at our meter under a [group captive / third-party] agreement that assigns the renewable attributes to us, as zero, and applies the CEA grid average to the remaining [Y] MWh as a proxy, because India publishes no residual mix factor."

example.title: Worked example: the disclosure figures for one year
lines: Consumption 2,400 MWh: 1,500 MWh contracted solar adjusted at the meter, 900 MWh from the grid
Location-based Scope 2: 2,400 x 0.710 t CO2 per MWh = 1,704 t CO2
BRSR energy table: renewable 1,500 x 3.6 = 5,400 GJ; non-renewable 900 x 3.6 = 3,240 GJ; renewable share 62.5 percent
example.note: Illustrative figures. The market-based total holds only if the contract passes the Scope 2 Quality Criteria.

senseible: Senseible reports location-based Scope 2 from the kWh on your bills at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, and market-based Scope 2 once you add the solar contract or certificate data, and its BRSR draft reflects the data you uploaded. Drafts are self-declared; Senseible does not check your PPA's attribute clause.
